Use histogram_sum(rate(rate(http_request_duration_seconds[5m]))) / histogram_count(rate(http_request_duration_seconds[5m])) to calculate the average observation size from a Summary metric in Prometheus during aggregation [C2].

When aggregating ratio metrics, treat the numerator and denominator separately and then divide the aggregated ratio instead of taking the average of a ratio or an average of an average, because that is not statistically valid [C1].
For example, when aggregating the _count and _sum of a Summary and dividing to calculate average observation size, keep the metric name without the _count or _sum suffix and replace the rate with mean, because treating it as a ratio would be unwieldy [C1].
Always specify a without clause with the labels you are aggregating away so you preserve other labels such as job to avoid conflicts and get more useful metrics and alerts [C1].
Also, when aggregating metrics, expose raw values and use rate(), irate(), increase(), and resets directly on the counter values rather than precalculating rates on the target, because that throws away information and can cause problems [C4].
If you need 100% accuracy, Prometheus is not a good choice because the collected data will likely not be detailed and complete enough for per-request billing, so use a separate system for billing and use Prometheus for the rest [C3].
Exposers should leave math or calculations up to ingestors because it’s a notable exception (for example, the Summary quantile is required for backwards compatibility) [C7].
Avoid exposing request failure ratios and instead expose separate counters for failed requests and total requests [C5].
Recorded metrics are not guaranteed to exactly match the original raw data, and aggregations in recording rules can produce results that differ from the original raw data, so shorter evaluation intervals improve resolution [C6].
PromQL recommendations for recording rules state that you should not expose a gauge with the average rate of increase over the last 5 minutes because letting the ingestor calculate the increase is better mathematically and more resilient to scrape failures [C7].
